_comment: The MVS instances on mvsdev.lan, and which of them a tool may submit to.
This exists because cc370 captured an oracle deck on port 8080 on 2026-09-10.
That is MVSCE-DEV, Mike's development machine, and it is off limits -- but
nothing in either repository said so. cc370 has no .env and neither does
mvs38src, so a tool needing a target borrows the nearest, and mvsmf/.env points
at 8080 because that is correct FOR MVSMF. The rule lived in one agent's memory
while every configuration in reach pointed the other way, and a prohibition
nobody can read is not a control.
JSON and not TSV, and that is also cc370's finding. The first version of this
file was a positional TSV with a header, and the header carried one doubled tab.
Ten fields against nine: a consumer indexing by header position read `submit`
out of the `pass` column, never saw "no", and would have called MVSCE-DEV
submittable -- the exact failure this file exists to prevent, shipped inside it.
An off-by-one in a positional format is invisible and total. Named fields cannot
drift.
No credentials here. They belong in a gitignored .env keyed by `name`.
The map is the part that must be readable by everyone; the credentials are the
part that must not.
submit=false means: do not send work there. Reading may still be wrong -- read
the note -- but submitting is never right.
msgclass is a CHOICE, not an observation: H everywhere because every tool here
reads job output back over REST, and class A is printed and purged before it can
be read. cc370 raised this -- capture.py defaults to A while mvsmf/.env sets H,
so a tool switching to this file would silently start putting its output
somewhere other than yesterday, which gets diagnosed as a missing job.

MVSCE-DEV.note: Mike's development machine. Never submit. The default in the mvsmf, ftpd, httpd, nsf370 and rexx370 .env files, which is correct for those products and wrong for anything here.

MVSCE-LAB.note: Produced the 5,528 reference decks on 2026-09-07 and is NO LONGER in that state -- SYS1.AMACLIB(IHADVCT) drifted. Submitting is fine; using it as an oracle is not. See docs/missing-macros.md.

MVSCE-EXP.note: Untouched MVS/CE reference; the control that LAB was not mutated.

MVSTK5-REF.note: The object baseline. Read only until Mike pins it as the oracle.

MVSTK5-BLD.note: Dave's build chain runs here. bldrun.py forces MSGCLASS=H so output stays readable; spoolarch.py keeps the spool flat.
